statement: Hypothesis 1 (Differentiation): strategic deviation is positively related to relative ROA. Tested by the first-order strategic deviation term in Model 2; the article reports the coefficient is negative, so H1 is not supported (H2 supported over H1).
supporting_locations: DOC01 p12 Table 2 Model 2 row Strategic Deviation
DOC01 p12 Results text, Model 2 paragraph
estimand: WLS coefficient on Strategic Deviation (first-order, linear) in Model 2; outcome relative ROA multiplied by 100 prior to estimation; weights from market share (error variance assumed inversely proportional to market share).
population: Bank-years of commercial banks competing in the Minneapolis-St. Paul (Twin Cities) metropolitan market, 1985-1992, Call Report data.
source: DOC01 p10 Hypotheses (Hypothesis 1); DOC01 p11 Analysis ('Model 2 added the first-order strategic deviation term, testing Hypothesis 1 vs. Hypothesis 2'); DOC01 p12 Table 2

statement: Hypothesis 2 (Conformity): strategic deviation is negatively related to relative ROA. Supported: the Model 2 coefficient on strategic deviation is negative and significant (p < 0.001).
supporting_locations: DOC01 p12 Table 2 Model 2 row Strategic Deviation
DOC01 p12 Results text, Model 2 paragraph
estimand: WLS coefficient on Strategic Deviation in Model 2 (same scale and weights as C1).
source: DOC01 p10 Hypotheses (Hypothesis 2); DOC01 p12 Table 2 Model 2; DOC01 p12 Results text ('The coefficient on strategic deviation was negative and strongly significant (p < 0.001). This result supported Hypothesis 2 over Hypothesis 1')

statement: Adding the first-order strategic deviation term (Model 2) improves fit over the control-only Model 1: change in weighted sum of squared errors 0.092, F = 30.4, d.f. = 1,954, p < 0.001.

statement: Analysis of the estimated Model 3 function indicates an inverted U-shape between strategic deviation and performance within the range of strategic deviation observed for banks in the sample (i.e., the turning point lies inside the sample range).
supporting_locations: DOC01 p13 Results text ('Analysis of the estimated function indicated the relationship ... has an inverted U-shape in the range of strategic deviation for banks in this sample')
estimand: Location of the maximum of the fitted quadratic, -b2/(2*b1) from Model 3, relative to the observed range of strategic deviation. No numeric turning point or range is printed.

statement: Autocorrelation diagnostic: first-order autocorrelation assumed; Durbin's h-statistics for all models were less than 1.28 (not significant), so autocorrelation was judged not a problem and OLS-type estimators consistent; no autocorrelation correction applied to the reported models.
supporting_locations: DOC01 p11 Analysis, autocorrelation paragraph
estimand: Durbin h statistic (asymptotically standard normal) for each of Models 1-3, computed with missing values inserted between banks so autocorrelation is not defined across banks.
source: DOC01 p11 Analysis ('For all models, Durbin's h-statistics were less than 1.28 (N.S.) ... Kennedy (1992: 140-141) noted that OLS estimators are usually the most appropriate estimator in this case')

statement: Heteroscedasticity diagnostic: OLS residual plots showed a 'megaphone opening left' shape against market share, implying error variance inversely proportional to market share; weighted least squares was therefore used and reported.
supporting_locations: DOC01 p11 Analysis, heteroscedasticity paragraph
estimand: Qualitative residual-plot diagnostic; implies WLS weights proportional to market share.
source: DOC01 p11 Analysis ('The megaphone opening left shape of the residual plot vs. market share suggested that the error variance was inversely proportional to market share. Weighted least-squares estimation ... was used ... These are reported in the results')
